Looping in infra/engineers. Summary of initial findings after 30m triage:
- We saw sustained token emission for most connections; a small class of requests (long prompt + tool-calls) hit a kernel selection path that currently disables continuous prefix flushing under high memory pressure.
- That path leads to long pauses where the socket is alive but no frames are emitted until the KV cache flush completes. Under bursty load the flush can be delayed >60s.
- The customer's logs show many simultaneous long-lived WS sessions from a handful of client IPs, which exacerbates the flush queuing.

Immediate mitigations applied (11:20 PT):
- Increased per-connection send buffer and reduced the flush debounce from 250ms -> 50ms for the affected model family.
- Temporarily routed Lumina traffic to a reserved capacity pool (dedicated small workers) to avoid cross-tenant memory pressure.
- Enabled an aggressive idle-heartbeat (ping/pong) and added a token-frame keepalive every 15s to avoid silent stalls being mistaken for live sessions.

We have attached the triage packet and a curtailed log dump. Please confirm if you still see gaps; we'll keep the reserved routing for 24h while we ship the patch.

Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: lumina_logs_peak_20280122.zip (subset), sla_delta_report_Q4.pdf
